summary: The W.G. Rhea Public Library argues that E‑Rate funding is essential to sustain its internet‑dependent services and programs, and that eliminating or reducing this support would force costly cuts to library operations and harm the rural community it serves. The library opposes any reduction or sunset of E‑Rate funding, arguing that such cuts would cripple its ability to provide broadband, digital literacy, and essential services to the community.
